articleBlocks: Tiger and Plane make the phrase structure visible quickly, but neither one tells you which word belongs in front. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Weight gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.

solutionNarrative: Tiger and Plane showed me that the board wanted a shared opening word, but not which one. That left me testing the structure without having a reliable answer yet.

Weight solved that problem. Paperweight is such a fixed everyday word that it immediately made paper feel right, and after that the rest of the clues turned into familiar phrases rather than tentative completions.
